source_verification_receipts.version: JASA 103(482), 2008 author manuscript corresponding to the published article
source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract and Section 1; published-record metadata at article head
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The article studies within-group interference under two-stage randomization and develops direct, indirect, total, and overall effects; its stratified-interference formulation is the standard anonymous aggregate-exposure condition.
Theorem 2.1 establishes complete randomization over a permutation group for any assignment vector and invariant estimator under the paper's invariance and quasiconvexity assumptions.

Hull studies bounded finite-population ATEs without interference, proves independent assignment minimax in that setting, and extends the analysis to arbitrary estimators through a finite convex program.

source_verification_receipts.locator: p. 6, Theorem 2.3; pp. 22-23, proof of Theorem 2.3
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 2.3 identifies the bounded no-interference minimax value with its binary endpoint experiment and constructs the bounded-outcome decoder from the binary minimax rule.

Proposition 2.2 represents minimax risk for the paper's ANI contrastive-effect experiment as a function of its conflict graph; its proof reduces to distributions over graph independent sets and relies on maximal independent sets being realizable by unrestricted binary interventions.
The paper derives bias and variance expressions for difference-in-means under a linear interference model and optimizes randomized saturation designs within that model-specific estimator analysis.

Kallus studies minimax-optimal mixed-strategy experimental design for precision, including an inference-constrained mixed-strategy design, rather than a bit-certified finite saturation orbit compiler.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Publish the 78-decision, 17-orbit, and 15-orbit rational tables with a content hash and an independent verifier transcript, so the strict-gap theorem is reproducible rather than supported only by a numerical summary.

Add a parameterized nondegenerate family of fixed-count saturation instances with a proved positive correlated-design gap, rather than relying principally on the two-cluster certificate and its contrast neighborhood.

Turn the compiler OEQ into a theorem by supplying explicit coefficient-bit-growth, facial-reduction, weak-SOCP, and outward-rounding bounds; this would make the optimal-design certificate operational.

recommended_next_step: Advance to Stage 0 with the exact-count hypergraph orbit reduction and certified correlated-design separation as the field-level kernel; preserve the compiler as the explicit first-class open construction.
